scope_findings.claim: The project builds one multisensory data-integration system over agricultural landscapes, grasslands and their ecotones.
Three omics layers enter the chain: metabolomic measurement from P01, genomic and transcriptomic sequencing and environmental DNA metabarcoding from P09.
The observation chain runs from in-situ plots through field spectroscopy and uncrewed aerial survey to Copernicus satellite data.
Three demonstration cases sit on one agricultural pressure gradient: farmland and grassland, the freshwater ecotones receiving their runoff, and the coastal transitional waters downstream.
Cases are selected for habitats and ecotones the topic marks as degraded or as restoration targets, not for data convenience.
The multi-season field archive is reworked into documented training and validation sets with a declared split protocol.
Deep-learning models scale habitat and ecosystem classification from the three cases to European coverage and predict trends.
Every map and habitat label the project publishes carries a crosswalk to the European habitat classification and to the global ecosystem typology.
Harmonisation workflows and processing protocols are published with provenance and linked to the open science cloud and the common data spaces.
Biodiversity indicators derived from the chain are carried into farm-management tools through an existing multi-country user network.
Effort and budget are earmarked for cooperation with the in-situ data collection frameworks the topic names, and project occurrence records are published to them.
Commission-steered grassland and agricultural-landscape monitoring data is ingested as a reference layer for the terrestrial case.
The pressures driving each case are analysed as socio-economic drivers, not treated as background.
Outputs are shaped to the reporting obligations the topic names, so a competent authority can use them without rework.
The project takes its harmonisation decisions to the standards bodies rather than keeping them internal.
A knowledge-gap and data-need analysis runs before the integration design, and sets which gaps the three cases address.
Predictive modelling is delivered at three scales, from the case sites through the regional gradient to European coverage.
The project delivers FAIR data, harmonisation workflows and processing protocols as named outputs, and verifies them on the three cases.
The assessment outputs are built for ecosystem assessment, protection and restoration planning.
Practitioner and decision-maker capacity is built through the protocols, the user network and the stakeholder work.
The project provides a standing coordination interface to the space-agency earth observation projects in the same cluster.
The interoperability work package holds an open place for the Joint Research Centre, which the consortium does not count towards any condition.

scope_findings.claim: Where a European research infrastructure offers a service the chain needs, the project uses it rather than rebuilding it.
